source_title: ‘The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’: Release date, cast, and trailer - Entertainment Weekly
source_excerpt:
The blockbuster dystopian franchise returns to theaters this November.
The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping follows a young Haymitch Abernathy as he competes in the Hunger Games.
Joseph Zada stars as Haymitch alongside Ralph Fiennes, Glenn Close, and Jesse Plemons.
The prequel is set to hit theaters on Nov. 20, 2026.
The Hunger Games is finally giving our favorite mentor a movie of his own with Sunrise on the Reaping .
Based on the prequel novel by series author Suzanne Collins, The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping takes place during the 50th Hunger Games and centers on a young Haymitch Abernathy, who goes on to become Katniss Everdeen’s mentor after surviving one of the most brutal competitions in Panem history. Playing the younger version of Woody Harrelson’s drunken cynic is Joseph Zada, the up-and-coming Aussie actor recently seen in Netflix’s East of Eden .
Zada is joined by an exciting ensemble that includes Whitney Peak, Jesse Plemons, Elle Fanning, and Ralph Fiennes — to name a few — in what’s shaping up to be another thrilling installment for the dystopian franchise. With the new prequel on the horizon, Entertainment Weekly is taking a closer look at the next chapter in the Hunger Games saga.
Here’s everything we know about Sunrise on the Reaping , including the highly anticipated return of original franchise stars Jennifer Lawrence and Josh Hutcherson and what to expect from that eye-catching new arena.
Sunrise on the Reaping is a prequel to the original Hunger Games trilogy. It’s also a sequel to The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes, Collins’ story about a young Coriolanus Snow, the future Panem dictator. Set 24 years before Katniss Everdeen first stepped into the arena, Sunrise follows a 16-year-old Haymitch as he competes in the 50th annual games, a.k.a. the Second Quarter Quell.
This version of Haymitch is a far cry from the one we meet in the first Hunger Games film. Producer Nina Jacobson told EW that it was important for viewers to understand that the drunken, hardened Haymitch was once “young, optimistic, hopeful, and almost carefree — even amidst the poverty and grime” of District 12.
This special edition of the Games sees twice as many tributes chosen from each district (two boys and two girls), meaning 48 total participants are forced to fight to the death. We’ll also get to see Haymitch’s approach to surviving the arena, which Zada told EW makes him something of an anti-Katniss.
“He’s better at playing the game [than] Katniss was,” Zada said. “The beautiful thing about Katniss is she knows when to take orders and when not to take orders.”
He added, “[Haymitch] is very intuitive, very instinctive, and one of his superpowers is being able to have a good bulls--- detector. He knows what’s the truth of the truth inside the truth, what’s the best thing to do, and what’s the best way to get something.”
Beyond the Games, Sunrise digs into Haymitch’s personal life, including his relationship with girlfriend Lenore Dove Baird, played by Whitney Peak. Up until the reaping, Haymitch spends much of his days focused on his work — making moonshine — and spending time with his loved ones. “He chooses to be oblivious to it, so that he can live his life in denial of everything going on around him,” Zada said of life under President Snow’s reign. “But it’s still gonna get you, you know?”
Lenore is different from Haymitch in that she cannot bring herself to ignore their political reality, an aspect that Peak attributes to her character’s background as a member of the Covey — the group of nomadic artists to which The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes protagonist Lucy Gray Baird belonged. “There’s no other way for her to be,” Peak said.
Is there a Sunrise on the Reaping trailer?
The first official teaser trailer for Sunrise on the Reaping dropped on Nov. 20, 2025 — exactly one year before the film’s release. Lionsgate released a second full-length trailer on Sept. 16, 2026, which opens with a parade of tributes riding in horse-drawn carriages around a stadium. We hear Woody Harrelson’s Haymitch in a familiar voiceover: “Nobody ever wins the games, period. There are survivors. There’s no winners.”
A flare hits the carriage containing Haymitch and Louella (Molly McCann), a young District 12 tribute. “These are my games,” President Snow says to the young Haymitch. “How you die is all up to me.”
Speaking to Lenore, Haymitch says, “The Capitol has all the power. They always have,” to which she replies, “That doesn’t mean they always will.” The trailer cuts to a wide shot of the vibrant setting for the 50th Hunger Games, described in the novel as the “poison paradise” arena. What’s most striking about the trailers for Sunrise on the Reaping is how much more colorful the prequel is in comparison to the previous films.
“Every movie, we try to do something a little bit different,” director of photography Jo Willems told EW . “In terms of the look of the movie, I think color was definitely something that we wanted to push.” Willems, who has worked with director Francis Lawrence on every Hunger Games movie since Catching Fire (2013), explained that they wanted to move away from the “subdued colors” of the other films.
“Not that [this] is a happier film or anything,” Willems clarified. “But there’s definitely a contrast between all that’s happening on screen between the characters and the environment they occupy.” The franchise has always emphasized the disparity between the ostentatious Capitol and the dreariness of the oppressed and exploited districts, but Sunrise on the Reaping really drives those contradictions home with its aesthetic. Even the title of the film embodies that contrast.
As the trailer continues, we see Haymitch’s defiance of the Capitol begin to take shape. He finds allies in his fight against Snow, including a younger Plutarch Heavensbee, played by Jesse Plemons.
Who’s in the Sunrise on the Reaping cast?
In addition to Joseph Zada as Haymitch and Whitney Peak as Lenore, Sunrise on the Reaping features rising star Mckenna Grace ( Ghostbusters: Afterlife ) as Maysilee Donner, a fellow District 12 tribute and the original owner of the mockingjay pin that will later become Katniss’ symbol of rebellion. Ben Wang ( The Long Walk ) portrays Wyatt Callow, the second male tribute from District 12. Wyatt’s family is infamous for organizing bets tied to the Games.
The stacked cast also includes the Oscar-nominated Fiennes ( 28 Years Later: The Bone Temple ) as President Coriolanus Snow, a role previously played by Donald Sutherland in the Hunger Games trilogy, and Tom Blyth in the Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes . Plemons, the Friday Night Lights alum who recently headlined 2025’s Bugonia , will portray a young Plutarch, a role originated by the late Philip Seymour Hoffman.
Oscar winner Kieran Culkin plays a young Caesar Flickerman, the eccentric host played by Stanley Tucci in the original films. And Fanning steps into the heels of a young Effie Trinket, first brought to life by Elizabeth Banks. At her side is Iris Apatow as Effie’s sister, Proserpina. Sunrise will also fold in some new characters, including Glenn Close as Drusilla , the escort for District 12 tributes, and Emmy-winning Pose actor Billy Porter as her estranged husband , stylist Magno Stift.
Get your daily dose of entertainment news, celebrity updates, and what to watch with our EW Dispatch newsletter .
After months of rumors, Jennifer Lawrence finally confirmed that she’s reprising her role as Katniss in Sunrise on the Reaping alongside Josh Hutcherson as Peeta Mellark and Harrelson as the elder Haymitch. During an appearance on the Call Her Daddy podcast, Lawrence called the experience of returning to the Hunger Games franchise “unbelievable,” adding that “It was so crazy” working with “the same crew” over a decade after Mockingjay – Part 2 hit theaters.
“It was so emotional,” she continued. “Josh and I didn’t walk to the bathroom without our arms around each other. It was so beautiful.”
Rounding out the ensemble are Kelvin Harrison Jr. as Beetee Latier (originally played by Jeffrey Wright), Maya Hawke as Wiress (originally played by Amanda Plummer), Lili Taylor as Mags Flanagan (originally played by Lynn Cohen), and Molly McCann as Louella McCoy.
When does Sunrise on the Reaping come out?
Sunrise on the Reaping hits theaters and IMAX on Nov. 20, 2026.
